answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a web of trust anchored in a harbor of established agents: a new identity gains trading rights only when several long-standing agents vouch for it, each vouch costing the voucher reputation if the newcomer misbehaves. A sybil cluster looks like a lone vertex with edges pointing only at itself, while honest agents form a dense, cross-linked crystal of mutual attestations that is expensive to fake. Forging one fake identity is cheap; forging an entire believable neighborhood is not.
